To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the socket is the most critical component of a limb prosthesis; (2) the socket is a complex system, which needs to be optimized in order to improve the quality of life of amputees; (3) the main open challenge is to achieve an advanced socket able, in real-time, to self-adapt to the stump, during static and dynamic tasks; (4) this objective can be achieved through the integration of different technologies and the development of new materials.

the socket is the key factor in determining the success of a prosthesis, and that the development of a new generation of sockets, able to self-adapting in real-time to all the factors affecting the stump tissues, is the most promising route to achieve a high satisfaction level of amputees.
the socket is still the weakest point of the prosthetic system and the main reason of rejection of limb prostheseses.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design and development of an intelligent, adaptive socket for limb prostheses, able to provide the best fit and comfort, while reducing the risk of skin lesions and improving the stability of the prosthesis during dynamic tasks.
the development of a novel socket able to self adapt to the residual limb tissues in order to improve the comfort/stability and, consequently, the acceptance of the prosthesis by the amputee.
the development of a smart socket, able to adapt to the stump and to its changing conditions in real time.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current state-of-the-art in socket technology is far from satisfactory, with the need of further investigations and improvements.
the current state-of-the-art in socket technology is far from the ideal solution, and the development of new solutions is still needed to overcome the existing limitations.
the current prosthetic sockets are far from being optimal and the development of advanced solutions, capable of adapting to the stump, is a challenging task that still has to be faced.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the socket of a prosthesis is a key component for a successful prosthetic fitting, but there are still a lot of open challenges that have to be solved to make the socket able to self adapt in real time to the complex inter play of factors affecting the residual limb, during both static tasks and dynamic tasks, in order to improve the quality of life of the users.

the socket technology should not be considered as a static device anymore, but it should become a dynamic and intelligent component, capable of interacting with the residual limb tissues in a smart and adaptive way.

the main open challenges in this field are: 1) the development of advanced sensors able to monitor in real-time the main parameters affecting the socket, 2) the development of new technologies able to self-adjust the socket in real-time to these parameters and 3) the development of a new generation of prostheses with a more advanced human-machine interface.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a more comprehensive approach to socket design is needed, which should include a better integration of the socket with the prosthesis, the use of advanced materials able to self-adapting to the residual tissues and the development of smart systems to monitor the stump and the socket in real-time.
, although a number of technological solutions have been proposed in the literature, a comprehensive and integrated approach to the problem has not been proposed so far.
a new generation of prostheses is needed, which can be able to self-adapts in real time to the complex inter-play of factors affecting the residual limb, during both static/dynamic tasks.
